blocks.text: Tomat provides managed focus sessions, pauses, breaks and a Waybar status control. The popup menu starts a reviewed preset, pauses or resumes the current session, skips a break, stops the session, and opens Tomat settings.

A session is owned by labwc-tomat.service in the user session and its break overlay is separate. Closing the menu does not stop an active session. Use Stop when you intend to end it; use Pause / Resume when you only need a temporary interruption.

Tomat notification, sound and overlay settings are session preferences. If a break is not visible, check the Waybar status and the notification quiet mode before starting another session. Do not run a second timer daemon to work around a missing notification.

Start session offers 25 / 5, 50 / 10, 90 / 15 and Custom. Settings → Reverse (toggle) swaps work and short-break durations for the three presets; the next popup shows 5 / 25, 10 / 50 and 15 / 90. Toggle again to restore the normal order. The choice is saved per user and applies to newly started presets without restarting the current timer. Custom keeps its explicit duration choices. Presets retain the configured long break and session count. Settings also exposes notification, sound and break-overlay switches. Open config edits ~/.config/tomat/config.toml; keep valid TOML and the managed hook commands.

A managed break can cover the desktop, pause currently playing MPRIS media, and open the managed Calendar and Agenda for the break duration. Ending, stopping or skipping the break releases its overlay and break-owned windows. Media is not automatically resumed. Use the visible Stop action to end a session before troubleshooting its configuration.
